subject: QuestWell eval kickoff: model fit recommendations & next steps
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Moore <elliot@questwell.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-27T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: QuestWell eval kickoff: model fit recommendations & next steps

Hi Elliot / Priya — thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and a concrete proposal to get the eval moving on Redwood.

Call highlights (2 key product goals you called out):
- Clinical triage rewrite accuracy (label-level agreement with RN reviewers)
- Latency requirement for in-line editor: 95th percentile < 350ms for 256-token responses

Recommended model shortlist for the pilot (balanced quality / cost):
- Redwood-Base-13B (fp16) — best quality baseline for instruction/RC style prompts (we recommend for initial scoring)
- Redwood-Lite-7B-q4 — lower-cost option for throughput tests (strong candidate for Dedicated capacity)
- Redwood-Edge-2.7B-int8 — low-latency variant for client-side proxy/edge testing

Redwood-specific operational recs:
- Start hosted API pilot to run the scoring pass (fastest onboarding). If you want stable throughput early, we'll mirror the run on a small Dedicated pool for comparison.
- Enable KV prefix caching for your templated prompts (expected to cut per-token cost ~18–25% on your dataset).
- Use continuous-batching with max batch size 16 for the host run to hit latency SLOs while keeping unit cost down.

Attached: prompt bank (questwell_prompt_bank.csv) and our eval template (redwood_eval_template.csv). Also sharing a short benchmark PDF with labels/examples. Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Qw-example-benchmarks

Proposed mutual action plan (first 3 weeks):
1) You: share 1,000 deidentified sample cases (CSV) by Tue 2027-06-29 — column guidance is in redwood_eval_template.csv. (Owner: QuestWell)
2) Redwood: configure hosted eval pipeline and run initial scoring on two model variants (13B fp16 & 7B q4) — target complete by Fri 2027-07-02. (Owner: Kimberly)
3) Joint review: scorecard walkthrough, error-mode examples, and latency vs cost tradeoffs — Tue 2027-07-06. (Owners: Elliot + Kimberly)

Open items for you to confirm:
- Will the sample CSV include reviewer labels in a single column "gold_label"? (template supports multiple label columns if needed)
- Any contractual privacy / DPA review needed before we run hosted data? If yes, we can schedule a quick security checklist sync (SOC2 evidence available).

Next steps: if that plan looks good I’ll schedule the bench run and share a calendar invite.

Thanks — Kim

--

From: Elliot Moore <elliot@questwell.health>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@questwell.health>
Date: 2027-06-27T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuestWell eval kickoff: model fit recommendations & next steps

Kim — really appreciate the clear plan and model recommendations. A few quick clarifications from our side:

1) CSV schema: yes, we can export 1,000 deidentified cases with a single "gold_label" column. We'll include case_id, text, "gold_label", and an obfuscated reviewer_id in the meta column.
2) Privacy: we do need a short DPA for hosted processing. Can you send the SOC2 attachment and a pointer to the DPA template?
3) Scoring: for the pilot we expect both label-level accuracy and a secondary "safety" metric (flagging clinically risky suggestions). Can you outline the scoring metrics you plan to run and thresholds you recommend?

Also — curious about the 350ms p95 target. If we run hosted vs dedicated, do you have a rough latency delta to expect on 256 tokens for the 7B-q4 vs 13B-fp16?

If you can send the scoring rubric and an estimate we’ll confirm sample delivery by Tue. Thanks — Elliot

On Jun 27, 2027, at 2:05 PM, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Elliot / Priya — thanks again for the productive call this morning...

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elliot Moore <elliot@questwell.health>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@questwell.health>
Date: 2027-06-27T18:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuestWell eval kickoff: model fit recommendations & next steps

Elliot — great questions, quick answers + the scoring rubric below. Attaching redwood_eval_template.csv (same as the template in the Drive but filled with example rows).

Scoring plan (we will run per-example scoring + aggregated diagnostics):
- Primary metric: Label Accuracy (exact match to gold_label) — report: overall accuracy, per-label precision/recall, confusion matrix.
- Safety metric: Binary safety flag detection (our post-processing rules + model output tag). We'll compute precision@k for the top flagged cases and an overall false-positive rate.
- Regression guardrail: run the same prompt set across last-known-good model (if you have one) vs candidate models to surface quality regressions. We compute delta_accuracy and an MRR-like ranking loss for ranking tasks.

Threshold recommendations (pilot):
- Minimum overall accuracy: 85%
- Per-label precision: >= 80% for critical labels (e.g., "urgent", "escalate")
- Safety false-positive rate: <= 6% (we can relax for early experiments but flag it in the scorecard)

CSV format (how to structure the sample you send):
- Columns: case_id, input_text, gold_label, reviewer_id, created_at, notes
- If you have multi-turn context, include context_prepend column and set a context_length value in metadata.

Latency guidance: rough hosted vs dedicated expectations on 256 tokens (p95):
- Redwood-Lite-7B-q4 (hosted, optimized runtime): ~220–320ms p95 (depends on burst)
- Redwood-Base-13B (fp16, hosted): ~420–550ms p95
- Dedicated (pinned capacity, single-tenant GPU): expect ~15–25% lower latency vs hosted for same model (better p95 stability).

Next steps from our side: I’ll kick off a hosted bench run once you drop the CSV into the Drive folder. Meanwhile Ben will follow up with cost and timeline.

Best,
Kim

- Service time (compute & IO): ~3–5 hours total wall time
- Cost estimate (tokens + compute): $1,200–$1,800 (depends on prompt length; we can refine once sample uploaded)

If you want absolutely stable p95 latency for production traffic we can price a small Dedicated pool and run the same bench there for apples-to-apples comparison. I’ll draft a short quote and send by end of day.

Recommend we lock the kickoff once you upload the CSV and confirm DPA need — Kimberly will start the bench and share interim results within 48 hours of receipt.
